request.spec:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Monthly period generation is in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass on `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:** you enter a from-date and a to-date and press the generate button. The app makes one period per calendar month from the from-date's month through the to-date's month. Each runs from the first to the last day of its month (so February ends on the 28th or 29th) and is named `yyyy-mm`. Each one is written to the audit file as `PERIOD_ADDED`, in the same format as adding a period by hand. A month is left out if its name is already a period or its days overlap a period on the sheet, and the other months are still made. The count of periods made is shown next to the button. A to-date before the from-date shows an error and writes nothing.

**What I changed:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate`, defined in `periods/generate.POST.yml`. It has two steps:
  - `ValidateGenerate` blocks users who can only view the sheet, checks both dates, and rejects a to-date before the from-date.
  - `GeneratePeriods` walks the months and creates each period, all in one transaction.
- **Store:** `Periods` has a new `addIfFree` method. It reuses the existing name and overlap checks but skips a month that fails them instead of refusing the whole request. No database schema change was needed.
- **Front end:** `PeriodPanel.tsx` has a new form with the test ids the spec expects (`period-generate-from`, `period-generate-to`, `period-generate`, `period-generated`, `period-generate-error`). Editing a field or pressing the button again clears the old count or error.

A blank date counts as the sheet's today, following the rule in `AGENTS.md`; the tests always fill in both dates, so that case isn't exercised.
